0.original: Wuk Lamat steels herself for the ride to find your next trading partner.

25.original: Give the fine hatchet to Wuk Lamat.

27.original: Deliver the verdant mate leaves to Miplu.

48.original: We've been doing so well! Even Tobli would have to agree...

49.original: Before we get moving... You should be the one to hold this.

50.original: With that, I suppose we should hop on the alpacas Mablu has so kindly provided...

51.original: If I'm going to catch a wild alpaca after this, I can't be shying away from the tame ones. Not that I'm scared of them, you understand. Or their nasty, disgusting, foul-smelling spit...

52.original: Ready to go? Let's mount up!

54.original: And it's off to the mate fields we go!

55.original: Please don't spit, please don't spit...

56.original: You'll be fine! These ones are accustomed to people!

58.original: You have a knack for riding, no matter what you say!

59.original: Without our alpaca friends, we Pelu would never have become traveling merchants. Can you imagine walking all the way across Tural?

60.original: I swear, that mountain is too tall to be real.

61.original: Worqor Zormor... Wasn't that the name?

62.original: A forbidding sight, isn't it? One I've never appreciated up close.

63.original: You have to take the long way around the cliffs to get there─to the highlands belonging to the Yok Huy.

64.original: So, Mablu, you said you were learning about the peddler profession. You don't care for ranch work?

65.original: No, no, I love it! I love working with alpacas!

66.original: But becoming a peddler has always been a dream of mine.

67.original: It's just... I'm not sure I have the talent for it.

68.original: If I can help you buy the taming saddle, though, then it'd be proof that I can do this after all.

69.original: In that case, you'd best get ready to be a merchant!

71.original: We made it...and without a single smelly incident.

72.original: I sent the alpacas back to Icuvlo's Inn, so we'll walk along the main road when we return to the village.

73.original: Speaking of roads to travel... You were adopted by the Dawnservant, weren't you, Third Promise?

75.original: Then perhaps you understand. I was an orphan too, you see─Tobli took me in. He took in all the ranch hands, actually.

77.original: Yes, and everyone works hard at their chores, grateful for the opportunity to repay the head ledger's generosity. Yet here I am, the only one wanting to go off and be a merchant...

78.original: I'm sorry, I don't know why I'm telling you this! We need to keep trading things for your saddle if you're to prepare for the Feat of Gold.

79.original: As it's mate harvesting season, they can't have too many quality hatchets. Add to that Wuk Lamat's way with people, and we should have no trouble making a favorable deal.

80.original: That's Miplu herself over there! Pass the hatchet to the Third Promise, and let's get to bargaining!

81.original: Did you give the hatchet back to Wuk Lamat? We should let her do the talking.

82.original: To what do I owe this honor...?

83.original: You have that little axe for me?

84.original: Thanks! Now to see what we can get for it...

85.original: You're Miplu, the owner of these fields? I have a mind to trade, if you're interested.

86.original: Well, well, the Third Promise! I might be convinced to entertain a proposal. What do you have on offer?

87.original: This hatchet! Forged by a seasoned artisan, the razor edge of this exceptional tool will make light work of your crops!

88.original: Hrm... The quality is acceptable, I suppose. I offer you a large sack of mate leaves in exchange.

89.original: A sack of mate leaves is valued at one pel in the thousands column─the same price as the hatchet. This deal would bring us no closer to the mezcal...

90.original: If I may, Mistress Miplu. It's harvesting season, is it not? Does not the demand for hatchets afford them a higher value?

91.original: It is indeed the season. Which is why I procured an ample batch of tools well in advance.

92.original: We've missed the window for demand... In that case, we'll have to fall back on connections.

93.original: Think of it this way! A generous deal here will put you in the Third Promise's good graces. Surely that's worthy of consideration?

94.original: I do not wish to give offense, but I must tell you that I stand with the Second Promise. His innovations will improve every aspect of our lives, I believe─including farming. And I will no longer have need of hatchets.

95.original: I assure you that I have nothing but respect for Wuk Lamat. That is why I'm prepared to purchase a spare hatchet at a fair price.

96.original: I-I suppose it <hex:021A020203>is<hex:021A020103> fair given your reasons. But we ourselves would be no better off for the transaction...

97.original: How about this, then. If we were to help bring in your harvest, would you give us a better deal?

98.original: As a matter of fact, I would! Until Koana's reforms come about, I can always use more hands in the fields.

99.original: Then you can go ahead and add our labor to the bargain!

100.original: Added value to tip the scales... How could I have forgotten one of the most basic rules of trading?

101.original: You can rest here if you like, Mablu. <hex:022C0DFF07022903EB0203FF02200203> and I have mate to gather!

103.original: Off to the fields, then, and mind you pick the healthy leaves. I'll take five good bundles from each of you.

104.original: I wasn't sure Miplu would bite, but it goes to show that you never know until you try!

105.original: Did you see how Wuk Lamat came to my rescue there? She really is good with people...

106.original: You've brought me some leaves, then?

107.original: An acceptable harvest. We'll see how your companions fared before I make any decisions, though.

108.original: Here, we've brought our share as well.

109.original: Thank you, Third Promise. This is more than enough to hold up your end of the bargain.

110.original: Now it's time to honor mine. After adding the value of your labor to the price of the hatchet...

111.original: I am prepared to offer you a full sack of our highest-grade mate leaves!

112.original: Premium mate! Bought at the shop, one sack of those leaves would cost no less than five pel in the thousands column!

113.original: Then we can bid farewell to this hatchet.

114.original: I'll give it a good home. Talk of the contest aside, I'm glad we could come to a mutually agreeable trade.

115.original: As am I! All the best with the rest of your harvest!

117.original: It's as I was saying before... Even after everything Tobli's done for me, I'm planning to abandon it all and become a merchant.

118.original: But then I needed your help after forgetting a basic rule of trade. How can I expect Tobli to accept my decision then...?

120.original: Have you mentioned your plans to leave?

121.original: So you intend to give up, then?

122.original: Not exactly. I wanted to prove I could succeed as a peddler before I declared my intentions...

123.original: I can't! After getting a taste of real trading, I want to be a merchant more than ever!

124.original: Then you'll just have to be honest.

125.original: I seek to follow in my father's footsteps, but not because he expects it of me. I want to preserve Tural's peace, and becoming Dawnservant happens to be the best way to do it.

126.original: You should live a life of your own choosing, and I wouldn't be surprised if Tobli held the same opinion. So talk to him.

127.original: ...You're right! It's better to find out for sure than worry over what he might say! Thank you for the advice.

128.original: But first, we have a saddle to buy. I want that success under my belt so I can be sure of my decision!

129.original: What's next, then? We try to trade our tea leaves for something halfway to ten thousand pel?

130.original: No, I think we're close enough now. I say we go straight for the premium mezcal!

131.original: Bargain our way into double the value, eh? Think you can do it?

132.original: Trust me! I will make this trade work!

133.original: I admire you, Third Promise. That you're holding your own against such strong competition for the throne is inspiring!

134.original: Uh... Am I really holding my own against Koana and Zoraal Ja...?

135.original: I-I mean, of course I am! I'm Wuk Lamat of the Dawn's Promise, after all!

136.original: Success! You traded a thousand pel hatchet for a five thousand pel sack of top-grade mate leaves!
